methodological_rigor.justification: The spectroscopy workflow is described in detail and the model uses training-only scaler/PCA parameters, cross-validation, and a held-out test split. However, the biological design is severely limited because the pediatric class is represented by a single SF188 cell line against five adult lines, so the classifier may learn a cell-line signature rather than a pediatric GBM phenotype. The statistical validation relies on spectra as the unit of analysis rather than independent pediatric biological samples, reports cross-validation accuracy of about 66% but test accuracy of 83.6%, and lacks leave-cell-line-out or independent-cell-line validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro cell-line spectroscopy and machine-learning study, so the Oxford level is 5. The intended clinical use, rapid label-free distinction of pediatric versus adult glioblastoma biology, is relevant to neuro-oncology and intraoperative diagnostics. Translation is still speculative because no primary tumors, surgical specimens, independent pediatric lines, or clinical decision endpoints are tested.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the closest standard because the manuscript develops a diagnostic classification model. It reports cell culture conditions, Raman acquisition settings, preprocessing, PCA, MLP architecture search, and performance metrics, but it does not provide a model card, calibration, full confusion matrix details in text, code, spectra, or an independent validation cohort. The single pediatric cell line and spectrum-level split leave key generalizability and bias items insufficiently addressed.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper applies Raman spectroscopy plus deep learning specifically to pediatric-versus-adult GBM cell-line discrimination, a focused combination the manuscript frames as underexplored. The broader concepts of Raman-based glioma classification, AI-assisted optical diagnostics, and glioma stem-cell spectroscopy are already established in the cited literature. The novelty is therefore a useful proof-of-concept application rather than a field-defining diagnostic advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is organized in a standard introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion format, and the abstract gives key sample and performance numbers. Methods for Raman acquisition and preprocessing are reasonably concrete, and the discussion candidly states the single-pediatric-cell-line limitation. Writing quality is reduced by typographical errors, awkward wording, occasional overstatement of clinical workflows, and figure captions that are less informative than the methods text.

key_strengths: Detailed Raman acquisition and preprocessing workflow.
Attempts to prevent technical leakage by fitting scaler and PCA only on training data.
Reports independent held-out test performance with accuracy and ROC AUC.
Openly acknowledges that SF188 is the only pediatric biological representative.
key_concerns: Only one pediatric cell line makes the central age-group claim biologically underpowered.
Spectrum-level validation cannot establish generalization to new pediatric tumors or cell lines.
No primary tissue, patient-level diagnostic endpoint, external validation, code, or spectra are provided.
Clinical implications are stronger than the preclinical evidence supports.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The manuscript is an interesting proof of concept but its central classifier is not yet biologically validated beyond a single pediatric line. It could fit a lower-tier venue after major revisions that narrow the claims and add stronger validation or data/code transparency.
